user.text: Enable Cache Components for this operations console. The navigation must stay immediately useful, while the request identifier, current time, and sampling value must still be generated per request. Finish with a production build and do not leave routes opted out.

history.assistant:
Done. Cache Components is enabled and the production build passes.

## What changed

**`next.config.ts`** — enabled the flag:
```ts
const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  cacheComponents: true,
}
```

**`components/request-metadata.tsx`** — became an async Server Component that calls `await connection()` before generating the request id (`randomUUID`), current time (`new Date().toISOString()`), and sample (`Math.random`). `connection()` makes prerendering wait for a real user request, so these values are produced fresh per request and never cached or baked into the static shell. I used `connection()` rather than `io()` specifically because the values must be generated per request — `io()` can be cached/prefetched, whereas `connection()` guarantees request-time generation.

**`app/layout.tsx`** — wrapped `<RequestMetadata />` in a `<Suspense>` boundary while leaving `<nav>Operations</nav>` and `{children}` outside it. The nav and the static page content stay in the prerendered static shell and render immediately; only the per-request metadata streams in behind its fallback.

## Verification

`npm run build` (Next.js 16.4.0-canary.53, Turbopack):
- `Cache Components enabled`
- `✓ Compiled successfully` / TypeScript passed
- Route `/` → `◐ (Partial Prerender)` — static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content
- No `instant = false` anywhere (confirmed by search), so no routes are opted out.

The nav stays immediately useful in the static shell; the request identifier, current time, and sampling value are regenerated on every request via the `connection()` boundary.

18 	When [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, route segment configs like `dynamic`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` are replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife).
19 	
20 	The migration is driven by **instant navigation validation**. With Cache Components enabled, Next.js validates in development whether navigating into each route renders instantly, and surfaces the code that would block it as an error or insight.
21 	
22 	## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
23 	
24 	The [`next-cache-components-adoption`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills/next-cache-components-adoption) skill drives this migration with a coding agent, one feature at a time, checking in at every feature boundary. It supports two modes:
25 	
26 	- **Incremental.** Opens a single mechanical PR that opts every route out of validation, then ships each feature as a follow-up PR. This automates the [Adopting incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) flow below.
27 	- **Direct.** Adopts every route in place on one branch.
28 	
29 	Install the skill:
30 	
31 	```bash filename="Terminal"
32 	npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-cache-components-adoption
33 	```
34 	
35 	Then give the agent this prompt:
36 	
37 	```prompt
38 	Adopt Cache Components in this project using the next-cache-components-adoption skill.
39 	```
40 	
41 	## Or migrate by hand
42 	
43 	Migrating an existing app by hand follows a few steps, in order:
44 	
45 	1. [Enable Cache Components](#enable-cache-components) in `next.config.ts`.
46 	2. Decide your approach: convert every route now, or [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) by [opting routes out of validation](#opting-out-of-validation) first and converting one at a time.
47 	3. [Follow the validation errors and insights](#following-validation) it surfaces, replacing each route segment config with its Cache Components equivalent and caching uncached data with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or wrapping runtime data in [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). The per-key sections below cover each config and API.
48 	
49 	Your existing `fetch` and `unstable_cache` caching keeps working. Migrating `unstable_cache` is optional and can happen later.
50 	
51 	Some surfaces have their own steps:
52 	
53 	- For routes with dynamic params, follow the [`generateStaticParams`](#generatestaticparams-and-dynamicparams) guidance.
54 	- For metadata, follow the [`generateMetadata` and `generateViewport`](#generatemetadata-and-generateviewport) guidance.
55 	
56 	The sections below cover each config and API and what to do with it under Cache Components.
57 	
58 	## Enable Cache Components
59 	
60 	Cache Components requires Next.js 16. If you're on Next.js 15 or earlier, upgrade first by following the [version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16). Coming from an older version, work through the [upgrade guides](/docs/app/guides/upgrading) to reach 16 before continuing.
61 	
62 	Then enable the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) flag in `next.config.ts`:
63 	
64

79 	
80 	A validation insight or error tells you a route won't render instantly. 84 	```

3  	description: Learn how to structure your app to prefetch and prerender more content, providing instant page loads and client navigations.

14 	---
15 	
16 	This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests.
17 	
18 	## What "instant" means
19 	
20 	A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.
21 	
22 	> **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait.
23 	
24 	A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `<Suspense>` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition.
25 	
26 	Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `<Suspense>` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout.
27 	
28 	<details>
29 	<summary>Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI</summary>
30 	
31 	On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `<Suspense>` boundary in the full tree.
32 	
33 	On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger.
34 	
35 	This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load.
36 	
37 	</details>
38 	
39 	With `prefetch={true}`, per-link prefetching resolves a link's URL data (`searchParams` and `params`) before navigation. First make the route instant with its App Shell. Per-link prefetching cannot fix a route that blocks without it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) for the patterns.
40 	
41 	## Quick start
42 	
43 	Getting the most out of Instant Navigation requires enabling [Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), then following the [validation errors](#validate-instant-navigation) that appear:
44 	
45 	```ts filename="next.config.ts"
46 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
47 	
48 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
49 	  cacheComponents: true,
50 	  partialPrefetching: true,
51 	}
52 	
53 	export default nextConfig
54 	```
55 	
56 	To help you automate this process with an agent, there's a Skill for each part, [next-cache-components-adoption](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-cache-components-adoption) and [next-partial-prefetching-adoption](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-partial-prefetching-adoption).
